title: SEP-0023 v1.4.0 invalid vector #15, claimable balance (B): Invalid claimable balance type (first byte of binary key is not 0)
caps_note: A pure encoding rule: SEP-0023 strkey text for a key type that no CAP in this entry's family introduced; the strkey group is cross-cutting
why: A published SEP-0023 vector that every decoder must reject (invalid claimable balance type (first byte of binary key is not 0)); a decoder that accepts it stores an address that is not the one the bytes say, or one that cannot exist.

reject.note: The claimable-balance payload's first byte is its type (0 = V0); 1 is not a declared type. The schema has no dedicated reason, so the closest class is used.

known_divergences.detail: Executed on 16.3.0, 16.3.1 and 16.4.1: the v16 StrKey decoder (unchanged since 16.0.0) checks the checksum but not the per-type payload rules and returns a payload. The strict decoder exists only on the v17 line, where 17.2.0 and later reject this vector.

known_divergences.detail: Executed on v0.7.1, v0.7.2, v0.7.3, v0.8.0 and v0.9.0: strkey.Decode with the claimable-balance version byte checks only the 33-byte length and returns the payload with the unknown type byte and no error; xdr.ClaimableBalanceId.DecodeFromStrkey rejects it.
